subject: radiology
title: Arterial Enhancement With Washout, Haemangioma and Focal Nodular Hyperplasia

steps.title: Washout marks hepatocellular carcinoma
steps.tx: **Arterial phase hyperenhancement** with later washout is the CT and MRI signature of hepatocellular carcinoma in a cirrhotic liver. The tumour draws new hepatic artery branches so it lights brighter than liver in the arterial phase, then its poor portal supply leaves it darker than liver in portal venous and delayed phases. That in and out pattern lets examiners diagnose cancer without biopsy in cirrhosis.
steps.say: Arterial phase hyperenhancement with later washout is the signature of hepatocellular carcinoma in a cirrhotic liver. The tumour lights brighter in the arterial phase from new artery branches, then turns darker as portal supply lags. That in and out pattern allows diagnosis without biopsy in cirrhosis.

steps.title: Haemangioma fills from the edge
steps.tx: **Peripheral nodular enhancement** that creeps inward is the haemangioma pattern: discontinuous bright nodules at the lesion edge in the arterial phase match blood pool density at every phase, then fill centripetally until the lesion is uniform. Small haemangiomas can flash fill completely and mimic cancer, but they stay bright on delayed images instead of washing out, and they shine very bright on T2 MRI like a light bulb.
steps.say: Peripheral nodular enhancement creeping inward is the haemangioma pattern: bright edge nodules match blood pool at every phase, then fill toward the centre. Small lesions can flash fill and mimic cancer, but they stay bright on delayed images instead of washing out, and shine very bright on T2 like a light bulb.

steps.title: Focal nodular hyperplasia keeps its scar
steps.tx: **Central scar** of focal nodular hyperplasia is a fibrous hub with radiating septa that enhances late, because it is fibrous tissue rather than necrosis. The lesion itself enhances brightly and homogeneously in the arterial phase from a central feeding artery, then fades to near liver density. Unlike adenoma it contains functioning hepatocytes and bile ductules, so it takes up hepatobiliary contrast and stays bright in the hepatobiliary phase.
steps.say: Central scar of focal nodular hyperplasia is a fibrous hub that enhances late because it is fibrous tissue, not necrosis. The lesion enhances homogeneously in the arterial phase, then fades to near liver density. It contains functioning hepatocytes, so it takes up hepatobiliary contrast and stays bright later.

steps.title: LI RADS sorts cirrhotic nodules
steps.tx: **LI RADS categories** grade liver observations in cirrhosis from definitely benign to definitely hepatocellular carcinoma, using arterial enhancement, washout, capsule, size and threshold growth. A lesion 20 mm or larger with arterial enhancement plus washout reaches the definite cancer category and is treated without biopsy. Subcentimetre observations stay in surveillance because most are regenerative or dysplastic nodules that declare themselves slowly.

A lesion twenty millimetres or larger with arterial enhancement plus washout is treated without biopsy. Subcentimetre observations stay in surveillance because most declare themselves slowly.

steps.title: Metastases wash differently
steps.tx: **Hypovascular metastases** from colon, pancreas and stomach cancers sit darker than liver in the portal venous phase when normal liver enhances most, the reverse timing of carcinoma washout. Hypervascular metastases from neuroendocrine tumours, renal cancer and melanoma instead flash in the arterial phase and can hide later. Knowing the primary tells the radiologist which phase to interrogate, and rim enhancement with a necrotic centre favours metastasis over primary liver cancer.

steps.title: Hydatid water lily in the liver
steps.tx: **Water lily sign** appears when the inner membrane of a hydatid cyst detaches and floats on the cyst fluid, wrinkling like a lily pad on CT and ultrasound. Intact hepatic hydatid cysts instead show daughter cysts inside a mother cyst, a wheel spoke pattern no tumour copies. Serology supports the diagnosis, and biopsy is avoided because spilling cyst contents risks anaphylaxis and peritoneal seeding of new cysts.

steps.title: MRCP maps the bile ducts
steps.tx: **Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography** uses heavily T2 weighted sequences where static bile and pancreatic juice shine bright while solid tissue stays dark, mapping ducts without contrast injection or radiation. It finds the level and cause of obstruction, choledocholithiasis and duct variants before any intervention. Endoscopic retrograde studies are now reserved for therapy, stenting, stone extraction and sphincterotomy, because MRCP carries no pancreatitis risk.

steps.title: HIDA and the cystic duct
steps.tx: **HIDA scan** follows a technetium labelled iminodiacetic acid tracer through hepatocytes into bile, proving cystic duct patency when the gallbladder fills. Non filling of the gallbladder by four hours, or after morphine augmentation, supports acute cholecystitis in the right clinical setting. The rim sign, a band of increased liver activity beside the gallbladder fossa, warns of severe inflammation or gangrene needing urgent surgery.
